plan: [ Second-price auction with independent private values (0–49). Dominant strategy is to bid true value: winning price equals second-highest bid, so shading risks losing profitable wins, and overbidding risks paying above value if the second-highest lies between value and bid. No prior rounds to learn from; single-round setting. Bids allowed in $0.1 increments. Therefore, bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit. [ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With value $6 and no informative history (single round), bid 6. If competitors’ top bid is below 6, we win and pay that bid, yielding positive surplus; if above 6, we lose with zero payoff. Overbidding risks negative payoff; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, bid truthfully at 6.0. ]

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding 17 ensures you win whenever the highest competing bid is below 17 and you pay that second-highest bid; if anyone bids above 17, you lose and pay nothing. No gain from shading or overbidding. One round, no history.
